from.place: proof, fourth paragraph: 'Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries; the matching covers of $U$ lift those boundaries after finite refinement'; 'the matching covers' presuppose the matching object M_n and the matching morphism K_n -> M_n of a simplicial object, here in a category with finite limits (applied to SR(X))

title: Matching objects of a simplicial object in a category with finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] and a final object $e$, and let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ with face maps $d_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $n\geq2$ let $D_n(K)$ be the finite diagram in $\mathcal C$ with objects $K^{(i)}_{n-1}=K_{n-1}$ ($0\leq i\leq n$) and $K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}=K_{n-2}$ ($0\leq i<j\leq n$) and arrows $d_{j-1}:K^{(i)}_{n-1}\to K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}$ and $d_i:K^{(j)}_{n-1}\to K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}$ for $0\leq i<j\leq n$; let $D_1(K)$ be the diagram with the two objects $K^{(0)}_0=K^{(1)}_0=K_0$ and no arrows; let $D_0(K)$ be the empty diagram. Then: (1) for every $n\geq0$ the diagram $D_n(K)$ has a limit $M_n(K)$ in $\mathcal C$ (for $n=0$ this is a final object, for $n=1$ a product $K_0\times K_0$), unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the limit projections; for $n\geq1$ write $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ for the projection to $K^{(i)}_{n-1}$, $0\leq i\leq n$. (2) For $n\geq1$ and every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, the map $g\mapsto(\mathrm{pr}_0\circ g,\dots,\mathrm{pr}_n\circ g)$ is a bijection, natural in $W$, from the morphisms $W\to M_n(K)$ onto the tuples $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$ of morphisms $x_i:W\to K_{n-1}$ satisfying $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=d_i\circ x_j$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$ (no condition when $n=1$). (3) For $n\geq2$ the face maps $d_i:K_n\to K_{n-1}$ satisfy $d_{j-1}\circ d_i=d_i\circ d_j:K_n\to K_{n-2}$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$; hence for every $n\geq1$ there is a unique morphism $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$, the *matching morphism*, with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\mu_n=d_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$; and $\mu_0:K_0\to M_0(K)$ denotes the unique morphism to the final object.
